messages:
kate.support: Customer (RedwoodCorp / acct: rc-482) opened a ticket: CSV export from Console -> Analytics -> 'Usage by route' yields 0-byte file or truncated rows when 'Include raw data' is checked. Ticket: SUP-2025-814. They attached two files: one 0 bytes, one with header and partial row. Severity P2, affecting 2 customers so far. Asking eng triage.
jordan.cse: happened to us twice this morning — first download was empty, second one had header + first row truncated mid-field. We rely on raw payload column for repros.
kate.support: Steps we reproduced in UI: Console > Analytics > Usage by route > set date range to last 7 days (includes today) > Filters: route=/api/v1/generate, granularity=daily > Check "Include raw data" > Export CSV. Request id in support logs: req_92b3eef. Attached truncated_sample.csv (link: https://s3.redwood.internal/sup/SUP-2025-814/truncated_sample.csv).
matt.eng: I pulled req_92b3eef from logs and reran export against staging with a dataset containing long JSON payloads (multi-line, embedded quotes and NUL chars). I can reproduce a 0-byte or truncated CSV when the payload includes embedded null (\u0000) bytes in the raw column.
- observed in worker logs: `ValueError: embedded null byte` and then the stream aborts.
kate.support: Customer confirmed their raw payloads come from third-party webhook and may contain binary attachments; they can't easily strip NULs. Any quick workaround we can give them?
matt.eng: Quick workaround: uncheck "Include raw data" (returns full CSV of metadata only). Also producing a manual export from internal support tool (we can run a job that sanitizes raw column) — I can run that for them.
sophie.pm: What's the root cause and risk? Is this a platform-level CSV writer issue or dataset-specific?
matt.eng: Root cause: our streaming CSV writer calls into the stdlib csv.writer which errors on cells containing embedded NULs when using text-mode writer over a streaming binary buffer. A dependency bump to the csv streaming helper (lib-stream-csv v1.3.0) made the writer stricter, surfacing the exception instead of silently replacing bytes. That causes the response stream to terminate before any bytes are flushed to S3/presigned URL, resulting in 0-byte file.
analytics-bot: Job analytics-export-worker failed for req_92b3eef (2 attempts).
matt.eng: Repro steps for devs:```
# fetch sample payloads
curl -H "X-Request-ID: req_92b3eef" "https://staging.internal.redwood/analytics/export?route=/api/v1/generate&start=2025-03-01&end=2025-03-08&include_raw=true" -o out.csv
# or run worker locally with sample fixture containing "\x00" in raw field
pytest tests/integration/test_export.py::test_export_with_nulls -k rep
```
I will open a PR to sanitize NULs before write and add a regression test.
kate.support: Thanks — I'll give the customer the workaround and offer a manual export while fix is staged. Can you cc me when a patch lands?
matt.eng: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/p/redwood/analytics/+/2329 — patch replaces NULs with the Unicode replacement char and falls back to base64-encoding raw payloads when customer opts into 'include_raw_base64' feature-flag. Adding test that simulates embedded nulls and long multiline JSON.
sophie.pm: Suggest we ship a short-term feature flag to return raw as base64 for affected tenants until we fully sanitize on read. Also add a note in Console UX explaining large raw payloads might be truncated.
deploy-bot: PR 2329 merged to staging and queued for canary deployment. CI: all green.
matt.eng: Patch is in staging, will monitor analytics-export-worker metrics for 24h. Targeting prod rollout in 48h after canary looks good. I'll follow up in this thread with post-deploy results.
kate.support: I'll update SUP-2025-814 with workaround instructions and ETA for fix. Thanks team :heart:
